moment: Princess Leia is being rescued from her cell by Luke and Han in stolen stormtrooper armor, and the first thing she does is criticize their plan.
prompt: Someone you barely know turns up to help you in the clumsiest way imaginable. Do you accept gracefully, critique them, or both?
followUps: Are you better at being rescued or at rescuing?
What is the most chaotic help you have ever received?

moment: Han Solo takes his payment and leaves the rebels to their fate. Then, in the middle of the final battle, he comes back at exactly the right moment.
prompt: Have you ever walked away from something and then changed your mind at the last second? What brought you back?
followUps: Would you forgive someone who left and returned like that?
Who is the person who always shows up when it counts?

moment: Luke Skywalker watches two suns set over his family's farm, certain that real life is happening somewhere else.
prompt: What was your 'two suns' moment, the point when you knew you needed more than where you were?
followUps: What did you do about it?
Is there a 'somewhere else' you still dream about?

moment: Han Solo is about to be frozen in carbonite. Leia tells him she loves him, and he answers with just two words.
prompt: Your partner says 'I love you' at the most dramatic moment possible. What is your honest reply, and what would your movie-worthy reply be?
followUps: Are you a say-it-out-loud person or a show-it person?
What is the worst possible timing for an 'I love you'?

moment: Han Solo flies the Millennium Falcon straight into an asteroid field while C-3PO nervously recites the odds of survival.
prompt: When have you ignored the odds because the alternative felt worse? Did it work out?
followUps: Are you the cautious one or the one who dives in?
Who in your life calculates the odds so you don't have to?

moment: Yoda tells a doubtful Luke that there is no such thing as 'trying': you either do it or you don't.
prompt: What is something you keep saying you will 'try' to do? What would it take to simply do it?
followUps: Who believes in you more than you believe in yourself?
What would you do tomorrow if you had zero doubts?

moment: Gandalf stands alone on a narrow bridge, facing something far bigger than he is, so his friends can escape.
prompt: What is worth standing alone against something terrifying for? Who would you do it for?
followUps: Have you ever taken a hit so someone else didn't have to?
Would you want someone to do that for you?

moment: As Frodo paddles away to go on alone, Sam wades into deep water, even though he can't swim, rather than let him leave.
prompt: Someone you love insists on facing something alone. Do you respect it, or follow them into the water?
followUps: Who would follow you into the water?
Is it more loving to respect their wish or to ignore it?

moment: At the Council of Elrond, everyone argues about who should carry the Ring. Then Frodo volunteers, without knowing the way.
prompt: Would you be the one who volunteers when no one else will? When have you said 'I'll do it' without knowing how?
followUps: Do you usually lead, follow, or quietly carry the bags?
What was the outcome of your biggest 'I'll do it'?

moment: Jesse and Céline meet on a train across Europe, and he proposes something absurd: get off in Vienna and spend the evening together before his flight home.
prompt: A stranger you click with asks you to skip your plans for one night. Do you say yes? What would convince you?
followUps: What is the most spontaneous thing you have ever done?
What would your perfect unplanned evening look like?

moment: In a café, Jesse and Céline play a game: they pretend to phone friends back home and describe each other as if the other weren't there.
prompt: Play it now: pretend you are calling your best friend about me. What do you say?
followUps: Was it hard to say it out loud?
What did you notice about me that you didn't expect?

moment: At dawn, with no phone numbers exchanged, Jesse and Céline promise to meet at the same station in six months.
prompt: Would you make a six-month promise with someone you might never see again? Would you actually show up?
followUps: Do you believe in fate, or in showing up?
Is a romantic promise stronger when it is a little reckless?

moment: Solène, a mother, accidentally walks into the wrong trailer at a festival and finds herself face to face with Hayes, a famous young pop star.
prompt: Who is the most unexpected person you have ended up talking to by accident?
followUps: How would you act if you met a celebrity crush?
Do you believe in awkward-first-meeting luck?

moment: Solène is in her late thirties and Hayes is a global pop star in his twenties, and everyone around them has an opinion about the age gap.
prompt: How much does age matter in love? Where is your line, if you have one?
followUps: Have you ever judged a couple too fast?
What does the 'right time' to meet someone even mean?

moment: When Solène and Hayes' relationship goes public, the whole internet has a say in how they look together and who she is.
prompt: Could you date someone whose life is watched by millions? What would be the hardest part?
followUps: How private a person are you?
What would you protect at all costs?

moment: At a village dance, Mr. Darcy dismisses Elizabeth Bennet, within her earshot, as merely 'tolerable'.
prompt: What is the worst first impression anyone has made on you? Did they ever change your mind?
followUps: What do you think people assume about you at first?
Do you give second chances easily?

moment: In pouring rain, Darcy declares his love to Elizabeth while explaining, in the same breath, how unsuitable he finds her family.
prompt: Have you ever given or received a compliment that was secretly an insult? How would you have made a better declaration?
followUps: Do you prefer grand gestures or honest, plain words?
How do you react when you are told something you didn't want to hear?

moment: At dawn, in the mist, Darcy crosses a field toward Elizabeth, the woman he once insulted, having changed his mind about nearly everything.
prompt: Can people really change for someone? What would someone have to do to make you believe it?
followUps: Have you changed for a person? Was it worth it?
What would you want to be forgiven for?

moment: Elinor Dashwood holds herself together for the whole story, hiding her heart to protect her family, until some unexpected good news finally breaks her.
prompt: Are you more of an Elinor (composed) or a Marianne (feeling everything out loud)? What happens when you finally break?
followUps: Who sees through your composure?
What do you do when you are overwhelmed with joy?

moment: In a storm, Marianne Dashwood runs across the hills, falls and twists her ankle, and a handsome stranger, Willoughby, carries her home.
prompt: Marianne follows passion; her sister follows sense. Which do you listen to when it counts?
followUps: Has following your heart ever gone wrong, or surprisingly right?
What would you do for a dramatic entrance?

moment: Colonel Brandon, a quiet older man, sends Marianne a piano and reads to her while she recovers: love expressed through small, patient acts.
prompt: Which says 'love' to you more: a grand romantic gesture or a patient, quiet one? What is the best thoughtful gift you have received?
followUps: What small thing makes you feel cared for?
What would you read aloud to someone you love?

moment: Jamie and Maggie agree it is 'just physical': no feelings, no strings. Both secretly suspect it won't stay that way.
prompt: Can 'no strings' ever stay that way for you? Be honest.
followUps: Have you ever promised yourself you wouldn't catch feelings?
What is the first sign you are falling for someone?

moment: Maggie tells Jamie to leave, convinced she is protecting him from a life of caring for someone with a serious illness.
prompt: If someone told you to walk away 'for your own good', would you? When is staying the loving thing, and when is listening?
followUps: Have you ever pushed someone away to protect them?
What would you want from a partner in hard times?

moment: Jamie is a smooth-talking pharmaceutical salesman who has never needed anyone, until he meets Maggie.
prompt: When did you realize you needed another person? Was it scary?
followUps: How do you ask for help?
What do you hide behind when you feel vulnerable?

moment: Thelma and Louise plan a weekend away from their ordinary lives, never imagining it will change everything.
prompt: If you had a weekend to disappear with your best friend, where would you go and what would you leave behind?
followUps: Who would be your Thelma or Louise?
What would you pack that nobody would expect?

moment: Somewhere along the highway, Thelma and Louise realize they feel more like themselves than they ever did at home.
prompt: When did you feel most like yourself? Where were you and who were you with?
followUps: What part of yourself do you hide at home or at work?
What would you change to feel that way more often?

moment: At the edge of the Grand Canyon, with nothing left to lose, Thelma and Louise choose each other.
prompt: Who would you choose, no matter what? And who do you think would choose you?
followUps: What makes a friendship that strong?
Have you told them?

moment: Bud White and Ed Exley, two cops in 1950s Los Angeles, could not be more different: one solves problems with his fists, the other with ambition and rulebooks.
prompt: In a partnership, are you the fists or the rulebook? What do opposites teach each other?
followUps: What do you admire in people unlike you?
Which of your habits drives others crazy?

moment: Lynn Bracken, who looks like a golden-age film star, offers to be whatever a man wants her to be.
prompt: Are we drawn to people for who they are, or for who they remind us of? Do you have a type?
followUps: Whose image of you do you try to live up to?
Who do you pretend to be on a first date?

moment: Bud White, a cop with a violent temper, realizes he is falling for Lynn, the one person who can see through his tough act.
prompt: Who in your life sees through your act, tough or polished? How does that feel?
followUps: What is your armor?
Who gets to see you without it?

moment: Alone with the Priest, Fleabag breaks the fourth wall again, and he is the first person ever to notice that she keeps disappearing into her own head.
prompt: Who notices when you 'leave the room' in your head? Who do you wish would?
followUps: What do you do when you want to escape a conversation?
When did someone last really see you?

moment: At a bus stop, Fleabag tells the Priest she loves him, and he gently tells her it will pass.
prompt: If someone told you your feelings 'will pass', would you believe them? Would you want them to be right?
followUps: What feeling of yours really did pass?
What feeling has not, however much time went by?

moment: In the middle of a chaotic family dinner, Fleabag turns to the camera for a knowing look, her only real confidant.
prompt: Who is your 'camera': the person you trade knowing looks with across a crowded room?
followUps: Who do you tell the truth to?
What is the last thing you wanted to say at a family dinner but didn't?

moment: On a long road trip, Harry tells Sally that men and women can never be just friends, because attraction always gets in the way.
prompt: Can a man and a woman (or anyone) be 'just friends'? Have you ever had to prove it?
followUps: Have you ever fallen for a friend?
Which friendship of yours broke the 'rule'?

moment: In a crowded deli, Sally proves a point to Harry in the most public way possible, and a stranger at the next table places an order.
prompt: What is the boldest thing you have done in public to prove a point? What is the most embarrassing?
followUps: Would you ever do something outrageous on a dare?
What would you order from someone else's table?

moment: On New Year's Eve, Harry races through the city to tell Sally he wants to spend the rest of his life with her, as soon as he realizes it.
prompt: When you realize you want to be with someone, how soon do you say it? Would you race the midnight deadline?
followUps: Do you trust fast feelings or slow ones?
What is the most romantic dash you have ever made?

moment: At the bow of the ship, Rose spreads her arms into the wind while Jack holds her steady.
prompt: What is the most free you have ever felt? Who would you want holding you steady?
followUps: Are you more comfortable at the edge or behind the rail?
What is the most daring thing on your list?

moment: Jack, a young artist, asks Rose, a woman he has just met, to pose for a portrait, with higher stakes than either of them admits.
prompt: Would you let someone you just met paint or draw you? What would you hope they see?
followUps: How do you want to be remembered?
What would you draw of me?

moment: Floating in freezing water, Rose and Jack have one piece of wood that might hold them both... or not. The internet has argued about it for decades.
prompt: Settle it for us: would you give up your spot on the door for someone you love?
followUps: What promise would you ask them to make?
What would you refuse to sacrifice?

moment: In his bar in Morocco, Rick, a man who 'sticks his neck out for nobody', sees Ilsa, the woman he never wanted to see again, walk in.
prompt: If an ex from long ago walked into the room right now, what would you do? Leave, stay, pour a drink?
followUps: Is there anyone you would rather never run into?
Have you ever reconnected with an ex?

moment: Rick reminds Ilsa that, whatever happens, they will always have the memory of Paris.
prompt: What is 'your Paris' with someone: a place or a memory you carry with you?
followUps: Where would we make our Paris?
Is a perfect memory a gift or a burden?

moment: On a foggy airfield, Rick puts Ilsa on a plane, choosing her safety and a greater cause over himself.
prompt: Would you let go of someone you love for the greater good, or would you fight to keep them?
followUps: Is there anything you would sacrifice love for?
How do you know when to let go?

moment: William, a bookshop owner, spills orange juice on Anna Scott, a world-famous movie star, then has to decide whether to say something clever or run.
prompt: What is the most awkward meet-cute you have had? Did you get a second chance?
followUps: How do you handle embarrassment?
What would you say to a famous crush?

moment: At a hotel press day, William pretends to be a journalist for a horse-and-hound magazine, just to see Anna again.
prompt: What silly pretext would you invent to see someone again? Where is the line?
followUps: Have you ever lied for love?
What would your fake job be?

moment: Anna admits to William that, behind the fame, she is just a person hoping to be loved. He has to weigh the risk of heartbreak.
prompt: Can fame and a normal life coexist in a couple? Would you take the risk, knowing it could break your heart?
followUps: How do you protect yourself after being hurt?
What would make you try again?

moment: Westley, a farm boy, answers every request from Buttercup with 'As you wish', which, in his language, really means that he loves her.
prompt: What is your secret way of saying 'I love you' without saying it? What would you want a partner's to be?
followUps: What is the phrase you use most with people you love?
Could we invent a code phrase right now?

moment: Vizzini, a scheming little man, shouts 'Inconceivable!' every time his plans fail, until Inigo Montoya points out that the word doesn't mean what he thinks.
prompt: Which word or phrase do you overuse, and maybe misuse? Which of mine is the most annoying?
followUps: Which expression do you want to retire?
What do people tease you about?

moment: Inigo Montoya has spent his whole life preparing to say one line to the man who wronged his family.
prompt: What have you rehearsed for years? What line would you say if you finally got the chance?
followUps: Do you keep old grudges or let them go?
Whom would you want to hear it from?

moment: Joel signs up for a procedure that erases the memory of his painful relationship with Clementine, and in the middle of it he changes his mind.
prompt: Would you erase a person from your memory? Who, and what would you lose along with them?
followUps: What did a painful relationship teach you?
Which memory would you never trade?

moment: Joel and Clementine meet on a cold beach and feel an unexplainable pull, with no idea they have met before.
prompt: Have you ever met someone and felt like you already knew them?
followUps: Do you believe in instant connection?
What was the first thing you noticed about me?

moment: Joel and Clementine, knowing they will probably hurt each other again, decide to try anyway.
prompt: Knowing how something might end, would you still begin? What is a hopeful 'okay' worth?
followUps: What is the bravest thing you have started?
Do you stay for hope or leave for safety?

moment: In a Tokyo hotel bar at 3 a.m., Bob and Charlotte, two jet-lagged strangers who can't sleep, find each other.
prompt: Who is the best stranger you ever talked to at 3 a.m.? What did you share?
followUps: Are you more honest with strangers or friends?
What keeps you up at night?

moment: At karaoke, Bob and Charlotte's shyness melts away and they sing what they can't say out loud.
prompt: What song would you sing to say what you can't say out loud? Do you sing in front of others?
followUps: What is your karaoke go-to?
What song reminds you of a person?

moment: At the end, Bob whispers something in Charlotte's ear, and we never hear what it was.
prompt: What would you whisper? Think of it in secret, then decide whether to share it.
followUps: Is some of what we feel better left unsaid?
What do you wish someone had whispered to you?

moment: Stuck in a Los Angeles freeway traffic jam, strangers burst into song and dance.
prompt: Where would you burst into song? What would your song be?
followUps: What song makes you feel unstoppable?
Do you dance when nobody is watching?

moment: Mia, a struggling actress, performs an audition song, a toast to the dreamers who feel like fools, and everything in her life shifts.
prompt: What foolish dream would you chase if nobody laughed? Would your partner support it?
followUps: What dream did you give up on?
Who first believed in your dream?

moment: In the final moments, Mia and Sebastian imagine an alternate version of their life: what might have been, had they made different choices.
prompt: Is there a 'what might have been' you sometimes imagine? Do you regret it or cherish it?
followUps: Would you swap your dream for a person?
What would be your 'other life'?

moment: After being snubbed by the staff of a fancy boutique, Vivian returns loaded with shopping bags to politely prove them wrong.
prompt: Have you ever been judged by how you looked or what you wore? Would you go back and show them?
followUps: What is the most dressed-up you have ever felt?
Which bothers you more: being underestimated or being judged?

moment: At the opera, Vivian, who has never seen one, is moved to tears by the music.
prompt: What was the first piece of art, music or film that moved you to tears?
followUps: Is there an art form you worry you would not 'get'?
What would you love to share with me that moved you?

moment: Edward, afraid of heights, climbs a fire escape to reach Vivian with flowers.
prompt: What fear would you face for someone you love? Which would be the hardest?
followUps: What is a fear you would rather not admit?
What matters more: the gesture or the effort behind it?

moment: Jonah, a young boy, calls a late-night radio show to ask for help finding someone new for his grieving dad, Sam.
prompt: If your child or best friend tried to set you up, would you let them? Who knows you best?
followUps: What would they say about you on the radio?
What would you want your match-maker to know?

moment: Annie hears Sam speak about his late wife on the radio and cannot stop thinking about him.
prompt: Have you ever fallen for someone's voice or words before meeting them?
followUps: What did you notice first about my voice?
Can you fall for a person from a distance?

moment: Annie and Sam agree to meet at the top of the Empire State Building, neither sure the other will turn up.
prompt: What is your dream place for a first meeting? Would you risk it on a total stranger?
followUps: Would you show up if you were scared?
Where did you first meet important people in your life?

moment: Baby, a shy teenager, carries a watermelon into the staff party and finds herself in a whole new world.
prompt: When have you walked into a place or a crowd where you did not belong, and loved it?
followUps: What is the boldest entrance you have ever made?
What world would you secretly like to join?

moment: Johnny, a dance instructor, teaches Baby a famous lift, practicing in a lake: trust built on balance between two people.
prompt: Who would you trust to catch you, literally? What does trust feel like to you?
followUps: Have you ever done a trust fall?
What takes you longest to trust someone with?

moment: In front of a whole resort of guests, Johnny stands up for Baby, and they dance together in public, no more hiding.
prompt: Would you stand up for the person you love in front of everyone? Has anyone done it for you?
followUps: What have you kept hidden for fear of what people think?
Where would we dance in public?

moment: Princess Ann slips out of her royal duties for one night and ends up sleeping on a stranger's sofa.
prompt: If you could leave your life for a day with nobody knowing, what would you do?
followUps: Who would you want to spend it with?
What would you do with a day of zero obligations?

moment: In Rome, Joe, a reporter, and Princess Ann ride a scooter and test a stone mouth said to bite the hand of liars.
prompt: Hand in the Mouth of Truth: what small, harmless lie do you tell most often?
followUps: Would you call yourself honest?
Which white lie would you never tell me?

moment: At the end, Princess Ann must choose duty over love, and she and Joe say goodbye in public, with almost nothing said.
prompt: Is it braver to follow duty or the heart? When have you been torn between the two?
followUps: What would you give up for duty?
What would you not give up?

moment: Amélie finds a childhood treasure box hidden behind a bathroom wall and secretly returns it to its owner, who is moved to tears.
prompt: If you could do one anonymous good deed for a stranger, what would it be?
followUps: Who did a hidden kindness for you?
What small things make your day?

moment: Amélie loves tiny pleasures: cracking crème brûlée with a spoon, plunging her hand into a sack of grain, skipping stones.
prompt: Name your tiny, private pleasures. Which will you admit?
followUps: What was the last small thing that made you smile?
Which ones would you share with me?

moment: Too shy to approach Nino, the man she likes, Amélie builds an elaborate treasure hunt instead.
prompt: How do you show interest: straight up, or through hints, clues and games?
followUps: What was the shyest thing you did for a crush?
What is the cutest attempt someone made to get your attention?

moment: Marty McFly travels back in time and finds his teenage mother, Lorraine, falling for him instead of his dad.
prompt: How would you react if you met your parents at your age? What would you notice about them?
followUps: What do you think your parents were like at 17?
What would you tell them?

moment: Marty has to make his shy dad, George, kiss Lorraine at a school dance, or he will fade from existence.
prompt: What push would your shy or nervous self have needed back then? Who gave you one?
followUps: When have you been the shy one at a dance?
Which moment decided something big in your life?

moment: Doc Brown tells Marty that the future is not set: it is whatever you make it.
prompt: If you could visit your own future for a day, would you? What do you hope to find?
followUps: What would you ask older you?
What would you tell younger you?

moment: Theodore, a lonely man, installs a new operating system, and within seconds Samantha has a name, a voice and a personality.
prompt: Could you fall for a voice or a mind without a body? What would matter most?
followUps: What do you value most in a conversation?
Would you date an AI?

moment: Theodore writes tender personal letters for strangers for a living, but struggles to write for himself.
prompt: Could you write a love letter right now? What would the first sentence be?
followUps: What is the best message you have ever received?
Why is it easier to write for others?

moment: Theodore learns that Samantha, the one he loves, is talking with thousands of others at the same time.
prompt: How would you feel if your partner loved many others as deeply as you? Where is your line?
followUps: Is love finite or infinite?
What does 'faithful' mean to you?

moment: Rachael discovers that her cherished childhood memories are implanted, not her own.
prompt: How much of who you are is your memories? If they were not real, would you be someone else?
followUps: What is your earliest memory?
Which memory defines you most?

moment: In his final moments, the dying Roy Batty saves Deckard, the man who has been hunting him.
prompt: Could you forgive someone who hurt or hunted you? What would make you save them?
followUps: When did mercy surprise you?
What is the hardest thing to forgive?

moment: Deckard tests whether someone is human by watching tiny reactions to emotional questions.
prompt: What single question would show someone is empathetic? Ask me yours.
followUps: What gives you away when you lie?
Which question would you not want to be asked?

moment: Morpheus offers Neo two pills: one returns him to his comfortable life, the other shows him how deep the truth goes.
prompt: Red pill or blue pill: would you rather know a hard truth or stay comfortable? When in your life have you chosen each?
followUps: Which truth was hard but worth it?
What comfort do you cling to?

moment: Morpheus tells a doubting Neo that nobody can be told what the Matrix is; you have to see it for yourself.
prompt: What can't be explained, only experienced? What would you love me to experience?
followUps: What changed how you see the world?
What would you show someone?

moment: Believing in Neo when almost nobody else does, Trinity brings him back with a kiss.
prompt: Who believes in you more than you do? How does that feel?
followUps: Who do you believe in against the odds?
What does it take to be believed in?

moment: Cooper leaves his daughter Murph to travel into the unknown, while she begs him to stay.
prompt: Would you leave the people you love for something that might save everyone? What would you need to hear before leaving?
followUps: What would you leave behind for them?
What do you owe the people you love?

moment: Far away in space, Cooper watches years of video messages from the family he left behind arrive all at once.
prompt: If you had to watch ten years of messages from loved ones at once, who would you watch first? What are you afraid to see?
followUps: Who do you miss most?
What would you want to record for me?

moment: Brand, a scientist, argues that love may be the one force that crosses time and space, even if we can't explain it.
prompt: Do you think love is more than chemistry? What is the strongest evidence you have seen?
followUps: Have you ever followed a feeling you could not explain?
What would you give up for it?

moment: Years later, Ross and Rachel still argue over whether they were officially 'on a break' when it all went wrong.
prompt: What old disagreement still divides you and someone close? Settle it here and now.
followUps: Have you ever been 'on a break'?
What rule would you need to state clearly in a relationship?

moment: Joey, famously, never shares his food.
prompt: What is your 'doesn't share food' rule: the one thing you are protective about?
followUps: Which food would you fight for?
Which annoying habit do your friends tolerate?

moment: At the end, with her flight to Paris waiting, Ross races to the airport to stop Rachel; in the end, she steps off the plane.
prompt: Would you race to an airport for someone? Would you get off the plane?
followUps: What would make you stay?
What big move would you want someone to make for you?

moment: Lorelai and her daughter Rory trade rapid-fire pop-culture jokes over breakfast at Luke's diner, fueled by coffee.
prompt: What is your daily ritual and your usual order? Which one could we share?
followUps: Coffee, tea, or something else?
What do you love talking about at full speed?

moment: Lorelai and Rory end the week with a movie night: takeout, a pile of junk food, and a rule that nobody judges.
prompt: What is your perfect cozy night in? What would we eat and watch?
followUps: Which comfort movie do you rewatch?
Who did you share your first favorite film with?

moment: Luke, a grumpy diner owner, and Lorelai, his most loyal customer, spend years circling a feeling that is obvious to everyone around them.
prompt: Have you ever been the last to realize you liked someone? Who noticed first?
followUps: Have you had a slow burn?
Would you rather wait for the right time or just say it?

moment: At school, Connell treats his relationship with Marianne as a secret, even though she is the only one he can really talk to.
prompt: Have you ever hidden someone, or a part of yourself, from your friends? What were you afraid of?
followUps: What changed once you stopped hiding?
What do you hold back to fit in?

moment: Years later at college, the roles are reversed: Marianne is popular and Connell is the one feeling lost.
prompt: Has someone's place in your social world ever flipped? How did it change how you saw them?
followUps: Who do you feel most yourself around?
Are you the same person in every group?

moment: Connell is offered a big chance in another country, and Marianne tells him to go.
prompt: Would you urge someone you love to chase an opportunity that takes them away? Would you go yourself?
followUps: What dream would you ask someone to wait for?
How do you know when to say 'go'?

moment: Daphne Bridgerton and the Duke of Hastings, Simon, pretend to court each other to escape the pressures of high society.
prompt: Would you fake-date someone to escape expectations? Who would you pick?
followUps: Have you ever pretended to be in a relationship?
What expectations do you feel from family?

moment: Lady Whistledown, an anonymous gossip columnist, narrates all the secrets of high society.
prompt: What gossip would you publish about yourself? What would you never want known?
followUps: What rumor about you was the funniest?
Who is the biggest gossip you know?

moment: Simon has sworn never to marry or have children, and holds on to that promise even as he falls in love with Daphne.
prompt: Is there a promise you made that keeps you from living? Would you break it for love?
followUps: What shaped your fear of commitment?
Whose rules did you inherit?

moment: Jim puts Dwight's stapler into a bowl of gelatin and looks into the camera with a grin.
prompt: What is the best prank you have pulled or fallen for? Is teasing a love language?
followUps: Who in your life would you prank?
What is the funniest thing at your workplace?

moment: Jim and Pam build a friendship out of tiny daily rituals: a prank, a look, a shared joke.
prompt: Have you ever fallen for someone through small daily things? Which rituals matter to you?
followUps: What small ritual do you want us to have?
Do you mix love and work?

moment: At a casino night, Jim confesses his feelings to Pam, who is engaged to someone else.

prompt: What would you tell your 'camera' about first dates? What do you really think while it is happening?
followUps: What is your worst date story?
What do you pretend on dates?

moment: Fleabag and the Priest talk about faith, love and why people feel the need to confess.
prompt: What do you confess to a stranger more easily than to a friend?
followUps: What do you believe in?
What would you confess to me tonight?

moment: Fleabag and her sister Claire love each other fiercely and drive each other crazy.
prompt: What is your sibling or best-friend dynamic? What do you argue about?
followUps: Who is the responsible one?
What would you do for them without being asked?

moment: After a loss, Fleabag keeps going with jokes that hide a lot of grief.
prompt: How do you cope with grief? Which jokes help, and which don't?
followUps: Who can you be silly with at a sad time?
What helped when you lost something?

moment: Elizabeth Bennet overhears Mr. Darcy call her merely tolerable at a ball, and instead of being crushed she turns it into a joke she tells everyone.
prompt: Someone judged you before knowing you. Do you laugh it off, plot revenge, or quietly prove them wrong?
followUps: Who underestimated you and got a surprise?
Did either of us make a terrible first impression on the other?

moment: Darcy proposes to Elizabeth while explaining how much he is lowering himself to do it, and is stunned when she refuses.
prompt: If someone says 'I love you' in the worst possible way, can you still hear the love?
followUps: What is the worst-delivered compliment you ever got?
Could you say no to someone you are secretly drawn to?

moment: Darcy writes Elizabeth a long letter explaining himself, and she slowly realizes she has judged him, and herself, far too quickly.
prompt: What were you completely certain about and turned out to be wrong?
followUps: How easy is it for you to say 'I was wrong'?
What first impression of me did you have to revise?

moment: Jane finds out on her wedding day that the man she loves has been hiding a huge secret, and she walks away even though it breaks her heart.
prompt: Is there a secret that would make you leave, even if you still loved the person?
followUps: What is the one thing you could never forgive being hidden from you?
Is walking away ever the strongest choice?

moment: Jane tells Mr. Rochester that she is not a bird in a net, she is a free person with an independent will, and he must treat her as an equal.
prompt: When did you last insist on being treated as an equal?
followUps: Where in a relationship do you refuse to bend?
Who first made you feel like an equal?

moment: Years later, after a long separation, Jane returns to Rochester on her own terms, not because she needs him but because she chooses him.
prompt: Is love stronger when you could live without it and choose it anyway?
followUps: What would you need to have built on your own before you could fully commit?
Have you ever gone back to something, and was it the same?

moment: Catherine tells her housekeeper that she and Heathcliff are made of the same stuff, yet she marries someone else because he is safer and richer.
prompt: Have you ever chosen the safe option over the one that felt like destiny?
followUps: What is the difference between a love that is comfortable and a love that is consuming?
Which would you choose at 20, and which now?

moment: Heathcliff, heartbroken, comes back years later rich and polished, and spends his life making everyone pay for how he was treated.
prompt: How do you deal with an old wound that keeps asking for revenge?
followUps: Is there a grudge you still carry?
What helps you forgive when you do not feel like it?

moment: Catherine and Heathcliff grow up wild together on the moors, running away from rules and chores the second nobody is watching.
prompt: Who was your partner in crime growing up?
followUps: What was the wildest place you used to escape to?
What would our teenage selves think of each other?

moment: Gatsby throws huge parties every weekend in the hope that one particular person will walk in, and checks the door all night.
prompt: What is the biggest thing you have done hoping someone would notice?
followUps: Would you rather be loved quietly or noticed loudly?
What would your Gatsby party look like?

moment: Jay Gatsby is sure he can rebuild the past exactly as it was, and tells his friend Nick that of course you can repeat it.
prompt: Is there a moment you wish you could repeat? Would it still be as good?
followUps: What from our past do you want to keep forever?
Can you love someone as they are now, and not as they used to be?

moment: Daisy lets the person who loved her most take the blame, and walks off into a comfortable life without looking back.
prompt: Have you ever watched someone take a fall that was not theirs?
followUps: What does loyalty really cost?
Who do you trust to stand by you when it counts?

moment: After graduation, Emma and Dexter spend a night together, decide to just be friends, and the book checks in on them every July 15th for twenty years.
prompt: If we checked in on our friendship every year on one date, what would each year say about you?
followUps: What does your ordinary July look like right now?
Who is your one-day-a-year friend?

moment: Dexter is busy being charming and famous while Emma, who loves him, makes a life in a job she hates and keeps waiting for her turn.
prompt: Have you ever waited for something to start while life was happening anyway?
followUps: Are you more a Dexter or an Emma?
What is the thing you want to stop postponing?

moment: Years later, they finally get together, and discover that the timing that kept them apart was part of why they loved each other.
prompt: Is there a right time for love, or do we only recognize it later?
followUps: Who would you have loved differently if you had met them earlier?
What do you want us to look back on in twenty years?

moment: At school, Connell hides his relationship with Marianne because he cannot bear what his friends would think, even though she is the only person he can really talk to.
prompt: Have you ever hidden someone, or a part of yourself, from your friends? What were you afraid of?
followUps: What would you not want your old friends to know about us?
Have you ever been the secret?

moment: Years later, Connell and Marianne keep drifting apart and returning to each other, mostly because they cannot say out loud what they need.
prompt: What do you find hardest to say out loud to someone you love?
followUps: What is something you almost said but did not?
What is the best way for me to ask what you need?

moment: Marianne and Connell realize that being with each other has made them better people, even if they cannot stay in the same place.
prompt: Who has changed you for the better, even if they are no longer in your life?
followUps: Can love be real and still not last?
What did we each change in the other?

moment: Noah writes to Allie every day for a year after she leaves, and she never gets the letters.
prompt: Would you write someone every day, knowing they might never read it?
followUps: What is the most romantic effort you have ever seen?
Do you save old letters or messages?

moment: Noah, now an old man in a care home, reads to Allie every day from a notebook that tells their story, even though she no longer remembers who he is.
prompt: What do you want us to remember about each other when we are old?
followUps: What story of ours would you read aloud?
What does loving someone who forgets look like?

moment: Allie has a brief moment of clarity and recognizes Noah, and they spend one short, perfect evening together.
prompt: If you had one perfect evening left with someone, how would you spend it?
followUps: What small ritual would you hold on to?
Who would you want to have that evening with?

moment: Louisa takes a job as a caregiver for Will, a grumpy, brilliant man who tells her he wants nothing to do with her cheerful dresses and her optimism.
prompt: Have you ever been the cheerful one with someone who did not want cheering up?
followUps: What is the best way to help someone who does not want to be helped?
What brings you out of a bad mood?

moment: Will makes a list of places he wants Louisa to see, so she will no longer be stuck in the small town where she grew up.
prompt: What is the one thing someone pushed you to do that changed everything?
followUps: What is on your 'do before you are 40' list?
Where do you want to take each other?

moment: Louisa has to accept that loving someone sometimes means respecting a decision that hurts you.
prompt: Have you ever had to accept a decision from someone you love that you did not agree with?
followUps: Where is the line between supporting and protecting?
How do you want to be supported when things are hard?

moment: Claire touches an ancient stone circle and wakes up in 1743 Scotland, with only her wits to survive.
prompt: If you woke up 300 years in the past, what would you miss first?
followUps: What skill of yours would be most useful?
Which period would you choose to visit for one day?

moment: To protect her, Claire marries Jamie, a stranger, and over the first weeks they slowly decide whether they can trust each other.
prompt: Can you build trust with someone you did not choose?
followUps: What was the first thing that made you trust me?
What does it take for you to rely on someone?

moment: Claire has to choose between the husband she left in her own time and the man she has come to love in this one.
prompt: Have you ever had to choose between two lives?
followUps: What would make you leave everything behind for love?
Do you believe in a love that outlasts time?

moment: Arthur Dent finds out that his house is about to be demolished, and a few minutes later the entire planet is, with the same level of paperwork.
prompt: What would you pack if the world ended in ten minutes?
followUps: Which tiny bureaucratic nightmare drives you crazy?
What would you do first with a towel and a day left?

moment: The greatest computer ever built, after millions of years of calculation, announces that the answer to life, the universe and everything is 42, and nobody knows what the question was.
prompt: What is the question you wish you had an answer to?
followUps: Is it better to know the answer or to enjoy the question?
What is your own personal 42?

moment: Arthur's friend Ford Prefect shows him that the best thing to do when everything falls apart is to keep calm, carry a towel, and have a drink.
prompt: What is your 'do not panic' ritual?
followUps: What is the strangest thing that calmed you down?
How do you act when things go completely off the plan?

moment: Young Paul is told that fear is the mind-killer, and recites it while a test tries to make him back down.
prompt: What is the fear you are most proud of facing?
followUps: What helps you stay calm when you are scared?
What was the hardest test you have ever gone through?

moment: Paul and his mother survive in the desert by learning from the people who live there, rather than pretending they already know everything.
prompt: When did you have to start from zero in a new place?
followUps: What did you learn from someone who knew more than you?
What is your 'desert', somewhere you had to adapt?

moment: Paul sees that the future he can predict will make him a leader who will cause terrible things, and he cannot see a way out.
prompt: If you could see your future and did not like it, would you change it?
followUps: Is it better to know or to be surprised?
What do you do with power you did not ask for?

moment: Winston and Julia meet in secret, away from the cameras, because in their world even loving someone is against the rules.
prompt: If every private moment was watched, how would you protect the ones that matter?
followUps: What do you keep just between us?
What does privacy mean to you?

moment: Winston writes his first honest sentences in a diary, knowing it could be the last thing he ever does.
prompt: What would you write in a diary that nobody would ever read?
followUps: What is something you have never said out loud?
What truth do you most want to keep?

moment: After being broken, Winston sits at a café and realizes he has betrayed the only person he loved.
prompt: What is the one betrayal you would never forgive yourself for?
followUps: Would you ever give up someone to save yourself?
What does loyalty mean under pressure?

moment: Bilbo Baggins, who loves his armchair and second breakfast, finds a group of dwarves at his door asking him to go on an adventure.
prompt: Would you leave your comfortable life for an adventure with strangers?
followUps: What would make it an adventure worth leaving for?
What is your 'second breakfast', the comfort you cannot give up?

moment: In the dark, Bilbo plays a game of riddles with a creature who wants to eat him and keeps his cool by being clever.
prompt: When has humor or cleverness saved you from a bad situation?
followUps: What riddle would you ask?
How do you keep calm when you are scared?

moment: At the end of his trip, Bilbo goes home a changed person, and the neighbors do not recognize the one who came back.
prompt: Have you ever come back from a trip a different person?
followUps: What did you learn that you would never have learned at home?
Where do you want us to go next?

moment: Harry, who has lived in a cupboard under the stairs, finds out on his eleventh birthday that he belongs to a world he did not know existed.
prompt: If you found out tomorrow that you belonged to a secret world, what would you want it to be?
followUps: What did you wish was true when you were eleven?
What was your childhood safe place?

moment: Harry, Ron and Hermione become friends after a troll incident, because nothing bonds like a shared disaster.
prompt: What shared disaster made you real friends with someone?
followUps: Who is your Ron and your Hermione?
What is the best friendship you ever made by accident?

moment: Harry looks into a mirror that shows him what he wants most, and the answer is his family.
prompt: What would you see in that mirror?
followUps: Is it healthy to stare at what we want most?
What do you want that you rarely say out loud?

moment: Katniss steps forward to take her little sister's place in a deadly game, before she has had time to think about it.
prompt: Who would you take someone's place for without hesitating?
followUps: What does it tell us that we did it without thinking?
What is the bravest thing you have done for someone else?

moment: Katniss and Peeta have to pretend to be in love to survive, and neither of them can tell anymore where the act ends.
prompt: Have you ever pretended something so long it became real?
followUps: What is the difference between acting and feeling?
How did we know it was real for us?

moment: Katniss and Peeta refuse to play by the rules at the last moment and choose each other.
prompt: When did you decide not to play by the rules?
followUps: What would you refuse to do, even if it was 'the game'?
What would you risk for me?

moment: Hazel meets Augustus at a support group and he puts an unlit cigarette in his mouth, explaining that you put the killing thing right between your teeth but never give it the power to kill.
prompt: What is your quirkiest way of dealing with something scary?
followUps: What was the first thing that made you notice someone?
What would you put between your teeth and refuse to light?

moment: Augustus uses his one wish to take Hazel to meet her favorite author in Amsterdam, and the trip does not go as planned.
prompt: Have you ever met someone you admire and been disappointed?
followUps: What would be your grand gesture?
Where would you take me with your one wish?

moment: Hazel and Augustus agree that they cannot choose whether they get hurt in this world, but they can choose who hurts them.
prompt: Who would you choose to be hurt by?
followUps: Is a short, great love worth more than a long, safe one?
How do you want to be loved when it is hard?

moment: As a young man, Florentino falls head over heels for Fermina after seeing her once, and sends her a love letter that is far too long.
prompt: What is the most over-the-top thing you have written or said to someone you liked?
followUps: What is the first thing you noticed about me?
What would the letter you wrote at 18 say?

moment: Florentino waits fifty-one years, nine months and four days for Fermina to be free, having a long list of other relationships in the meantime.
prompt: How long would you wait for someone?
followUps: Is waiting romantic or is it avoiding the present?
What would you say to your waiting self?

moment: When they finally meet again as old people, they start a slow, funny, tender courtship over letters and walks.
prompt: What do you think love looks like at 70?

What do you hope stays the same about us?

moment: In the town of Macondo, a father takes his young son to discover ice, and the boy remembers that afternoon for the rest of his life.
prompt: What is the first 'magic' thing you remember from childhood?
followUps: Which small wonder do you still remember vividly?
What would you show someone for the first time?

moment: The Buendía family keeps naming the children after their ancestors and repeating the same mistakes across generations.
prompt: Which family pattern do you recognize in yourself?
followUps: What do you want to do differently from your parents?
Which tradition of yours do you want to keep?

moment: A young woman, Remedios the Beauty, is so unaffected by the world that she simply floats up into the sky one afternoon while hanging the laundry.
prompt: If you could disappear into thin air, would you?
followUps: What would you leave behind?
When do you most want to escape the ordinary?

prompt: What would you tell your younger self if you had five minutes?
followUps: What would it be like to meet someone who already knows you?
If you could visit one moment in our past, which would it be?

moment: Henry vanishes without warning, again and again, and Clare learns to live with long waits and sudden returns.
prompt: How do you cope with someone being unavailable?
followUps: What helps you wait?
What does reliability mean to you?

moment: Knowing how their story ends, Clare and Henry choose to make every present moment count anyway.
prompt: If you knew how our story ends, would you want to know?
followUps: What would you do differently if you knew time was short?
What is the moment you want to hold onto?

moment: On their fifth anniversary, Nick comes home to find his wife Amy missing and a living room that looks like a crime scene, and the first thing everybody sees is his awkward smile.
prompt: How do you react in a crisis, and how does it look to others?
followUps: What do people misread about you?
Do you think you know me completely?

moment: Amy's diary shows a marriage that started as a perfect game and slowly turned into two people performing for each other.
prompt: Do you ever perform in front of the person you love?
followUps: What is the 'cool' version of yourself you used to show on early dates?
When did you stop pretending with me?

moment: Nick and Amy, who understand each other better than anyone, stay together because each knows exactly what the other is capable of.
prompt: Is knowing someone completely a comfort or a threat?
followUps: What is the thing you hope I will never find out?
What is the difference between trust and being trapped?

moment: Bridget starts her year with resolutions to lose weight, drink less and find a sensible boyfriend, and logs every failure with total honesty.
prompt: What is the resolution you break every year?
followUps: What would your honest diary say about today?
What would you like to be better at?

moment: Bridget meets Mark Darcy at a party where she is wearing a ridiculous outfit, and the first conversation goes terribly.
prompt: What is your most embarrassing first impression?
followUps: Did we start badly and become better?
What is the outfit you would like to forget?

moment: Mark tells Bridget that he likes her just as she is, with all of her flaws.
prompt: What is the best thing someone has said about the real you?
followUps: What do you most want to be liked for?
Which of my flaws do you secretly love?

moment: A pilot stranded in the desert meets a boy who asks him to draw a sheep, and takes his time to accept anything the pilot draws.
prompt: What do grown-ups misunderstand that kids see clearly?

When did you last see something like a child would?

followUps: What does it mean to take someone's time and make them yours?
What have we 'tamed' in each other?

prompt: What is something you have invested time in that matters because of that time?
followUps: What are you responsible for?
What is the quiet routine of ours you would miss?

moment: Scout is told by her father that you never really understand a person until you climb into his skin and walk around in it.
prompt: Whose skin would you like to walk around in for a day?
followUps: Who did you misjudge before getting to know them?
How do we practice understanding each other?

moment: Atticus Finch takes on a case he knows he will lose, because it is the right thing to do.
prompt: When did you do something right knowing you would lose?
followUps: What is the cause you would stand for?
Who is your Atticus?

moment: The neighbor the children feared turns out to be the one who watched over them all along.
prompt: Who did you fear that turned out to be kind?
followUps: What did you misread as a kid?
Who is looking out for you without you noticing?

moment: Santiago, a shepherd, keeps having a dream about treasure in the pyramids and decides to sell his flock and go.

followUps: What is the thing you keep dreaming of?
What stops you?

followUps: What was your biggest 'day one' failure?
What gets you up again?

prompt: Have you ever found what you were looking for at home?
followUps: Would you have valued it if you had not left?
What is your 'home treasure'?

moment: Anna and Vronsky meet at a train station and the attraction is immediate, even though she is married and has a son.
prompt: Can you control who you fall for?
followUps: Where is the line between a spark and a choice?
What would you do if you felt a spark with someone else?

moment: While Anna's love story burns, Levin, a quiet landowner, slowly builds a good marriage with Kitty full of ordinary patience.
prompt: Are you more a Levin or a Vronsky about love?
followUps: Is stability boring or the best part?
What small things do you cherish in daily life?

moment: Anna realizes that being cut off from society for the sake of love is making her suspicious and lonely.
prompt: Does love need friends and family to survive?
followUps: What would you give up for love?
What would you never give up?

moment: Patroclus, a shy boy sent away in disgrace, is befriended by golden Achilles, and they spend years growing up together.
prompt: Who befriended you when you felt like an outsider?
followUps: What did you need most at that time?
Who has been a lifelong friend for you?

moment: Achilles has to choose between a short life of glory and a long one of peace, and tells Patroclus that he wants to be remembered with him.
prompt: Would you rather be famous or happy?
followUps: What do you want to be remembered for?
Who do you want to be remembered next to?

moment: Patroclus remains with Achilles even in death, and the story is told as a promise to keep his name alive.
prompt: Whose story do you want to keep alive?
followUps: What do you want people to say about us?
What do you want to leave behind?

moment: An aging Hollywood star, Evelyn Hugo, picks an unknown journalist to write her life story and refuses to explain why.
prompt: If you could tell your whole story to one stranger, who would you pick?
followUps: What chapter of your life would be the longest?
What would the title of your autobiography be?

moment: Evelyn marries seven times, and each marriage was a strategy, except the love of her life, which she had to keep secret for decades.
prompt: Have you ever hidden what mattered most to you?
followUps: What would you do differently if no one was watching?
What is the strategy you regret?

moment: Evelyn reveals why she chose this journalist, and why her last story was meant to be told now.
prompt: What do you want to be honest about before it is too late?
followUps: What is a story you want to tell your future self?
What is something you have kept to yourself too long?

moment: Eleanor eats the same meal deal every day, talks to nobody over the weekend, and describes her life as completely fine.
prompt: What does 'I am fine' really mean when you say it?
followUps: What is your most predictable routine?
How would you notice if I was not fine?

moment: A kind colleague, Raymond, helps an old man who collapses in the street, and slowly brings Eleanor into a friendship she did not know she needed.
prompt: Who showed up for you without being asked?
followUps: What makes someone feel like a safe person?
What is the smallest kindness you remember?

moment: Eleanor finally lets herself ask for help, and discovers that being looked after does not make her weak.
prompt: When did you last ask for help?
followUps: What is hard about it for you?
How can I help you without making you feel small?

moment: The four March sisters stage plays in the attic on Christmas Eve, writing, directing and fighting over the best roles.
prompt: What did you do with your siblings or friends at home as a kid?
followUps: What was your childhood 'play' or game?
What holiday tradition do you want to keep for our family?

moment: Jo refuses to marry her neighbor Laurie, even though everyone thinks she should, because she does not love him that way.
prompt: Have you ever said no to something that looked perfect on paper?
followUps: What do other people expect of you that you have not wanted?
How do you know when someone is not right for you?

moment: Jo, who always wanted to be independent, falls for an older, quiet professor who values her writing and her honesty.
prompt: Who valued your talents before you did?
followUps: What kind of partner challenges you in a good way?
What do you want to be supported in?

moment: Ned Stark takes his children to watch the execution of a deserter, and teaches his son that the man who passes the sentence should swing the sword.
prompt: Do you think someone who gives orders should be willing to carry them out?
followUps: What did your parents teach you about responsibility?
What is a lesson from your childhood you still follow?

moment: Ned has to choose between his duty to the king and the safety of his daughters, and both options cost him something.
prompt: Have you had to choose between duty and family?
followUps: What would you put first?
How do we decide when our values compete?

moment: Daenerys, married off to a warlord she is afraid of, slowly finds her strength and takes control of her own story.
prompt: When did you discover a strength you did not know you had?
followUps: Who helped you grow into yourself?
What is your own 'take control' moment?

moment: Elio spends a summer at his family's villa in Italy, and the visiting student, Oliver, becomes the one thing he cannot stop thinking about.
prompt: What was your most intense summer crush?

What did we each do with our early crushes?

moment: Elio and Oliver spend days pretending to be indifferent, and nights seeing each other's real side.
prompt: Do you hide your feelings or show them? Why?
followUps: What is the safest way to say 'I like you'?
What was the first sign that you liked me?

moment: After Oliver leaves, Elio's father tells him that to feel nothing so as not to feel pain is to waste your life.
prompt: What is the best advice a parent gave you about heartbreak?
followUps: Would you rather feel everything or protect yourself?
What do you want to feel more of?

moment: A young woman marries a wealthy widower, moves into his enormous house, and finds that everyone still talks about his first wife as if she were in the next room.
prompt: How do you deal with comparison to someone else, even a ghost?
followUps: Who in my past do you secretly wonder about?
What would you want to ask my ex?

moment: The housekeeper, Mrs. Danvers, quietly tries to make the new Mrs. de Winter feel small in every room of the house.
prompt: Have you ever felt unwelcome somewhere you were supposed to feel at home?
followUps: How do you handle someone who is passive-aggressive?
Who has made you feel small?

moment: The narrator realizes she has been afraid of a version of the first wife that was never true, and that her husband loves her more than she thought.
prompt: What fear did you believe for too long?
followUps: What did you find out about me that surprised you?
What do you believe about yourself that may not be true?

prompt: Before meeting a partner's family for the first time, what is the one question you really want answered?
followUps: What worried you the first time you met someone's parents?
What should a partner warn you about before you meet their family?

prompt: When something feels off and the person you love says it's fine, who do you trust: them or your gut?
followUps: Have you ever been told you were overreacting and turned out to be right?
How should a partner react when you say 'something feels wrong'?

moment: Chris realizes too late that the person who was supposed to protect him knew everything all along.
prompt: What kind of betrayal could you never come back from?
followUps: What makes you feel truly safe with someone?
Which warning signs have you learned to take seriously?

moment: Jack takes a job looking after an empty mountain hotel all winter, sure that months of snowy quiet will finally let him write.
