followUps: What project would you finally finish?
How long before we drove each other crazy?

moment: Wendy finds the pages Jack has been typing for weeks, and every page repeats the same sentence over and over.
prompt: What is a sign that someone you love is not okay, even when they say they are?
followUps: How do you usually show that you are struggling?
What would you want me to do if I noticed?

moment: Cut off from everyone and exhausted, Jack slowly turns his frustration on the people closest to him.
prompt: How do you keep stress from landing on the people you love?
followUps: Who usually gets the worst of your bad days?
What helps you reset before you snap?

moment: In a world where any sound can be deadly, the Abbott family walks barefoot on paths of sand and talks only in sign language.
prompt: If we couldn't speak out loud for a month, how would we communicate? What would we invent?
followUps: What could you tell me with just a look?
Which of our habits would be hardest to do in silence?

moment: Lee takes his son to a roaring waterfall, the only place where they can safely talk out loud, and his son asks why he never tells his daughter he loves her.
prompt: Is there something you assume people know, but never actually say out loud?
followUps: Who in your family said 'I love you' easily, and who never did?
What would you say if you had one minute to speak freely?

moment: Evelyn and Lee slow dance in their silent house to one song shared through a pair of earbuds.
prompt: What song would you choose for one silent dance together?
followUps: What small ritual keeps you close when life is hard?
When did a tiny moment feel bigger than it was?

moment: The Kim family, crammed into a half-basement flat, fold pizza boxes for cash and wander around the bathroom chasing a free wifi signal.
prompt: What is the most creative thing you have done to get by when money was tight?
followUps: What was your very first job?
Which small luxury would you give up last?

moment: Ki-woo gets a tutoring job in a rich family's glass house with a fake diploma, and one by one his whole family follows him in under false identities.
prompt: Would you lie on your CV for a dream job? Where is your line?
followUps: Have you ever pretended to be more qualified than you were?
Would you forgive a partner whose career started with a lie?

moment: The wealthy father keeps remarking that his driver has a certain smell, and the comment lands like a slap.
prompt: Have you ever been made to feel you didn't belong somewhere? How did you react?
followUps: Which small comments have stayed with you for years?
How do you notice when you make someone feel small?

moment: Marta, the nurse of a rich crime novelist, physically throws up whenever she lies, which makes her the worst possible person to keep a secret.
prompt: What's your tell when you lie? Do you think I would notice?
followUps: What's the last white lie you told?
Is there a lie you think is always okay?

moment: After the old man's death, every member of his family insists they were his favorite and that they built their success all by themselves.
prompt: What story does your family tell about itself that isn't entirely true?
followUps: Who is the favorite in your family, honestly?
What would our family reunion argue about?

moment: Harlan leaves everything to Marta, the one person who was kind to him without wanting anything back.
prompt: Who has been kind to you without wanting anything in return?
followUps: How do you thank people like that?
Would you accept a huge gift that someone's family thought was theirs?

moment: Vincent has to take his boss's wife Mia out for one evening, and they end up in a twist contest at a retro diner.
prompt: If we entered a dance contest tonight, what would our routine be?
followUps: What's your go-to dance move?
What's the strangest place you've ever danced?

moment: Over dinner, Mia asks Vincent whether silences are uncomfortable, or whether you only feel at ease in silence with someone special.
prompt: Can you be quiet with someone and feel comfortable? When did you first feel that with me?
followUps: Who do you always feel the need to fill silences with?
What does a comfortable silence feel like to you?

moment: After surviving something that should have killed him, Jules decides it was a sign and quits his old life on the spot.
prompt: Have you ever had a moment that changed your direction overnight?
followUps: Do you believe in signs?
What would it take for you to walk away from your current life?

moment: On his daughter's wedding day, Don Corleone receives guests one by one in his office, because tradition says he cannot refuse a request on that day.
prompt: Which favor would you never refuse a friend, no matter what?
followUps: Who would you ask for a big favor without hesitating?
Do you keep score of favors?

moment: Michael, the son who wanted nothing to do with the family business, steps in when his father is in danger, and slowly becomes what he swore he never would.
prompt: What did you promise yourself you would never become? How is that going?
followUps: Which of your parents' habits do you see in yourself?
What family role did you end up taking even though you didn't want it?

moment: Michael lies to his wife Kay's face about what he has done, and a door literally closes between them.
prompt: Is there a kind of secret a partner should never keep, even to protect you?
followUps: Would you rather know a painful truth or be protected from it?
What would you do if you saw that door close?

moment: FBI trainee Clarice Starling needs help from a brilliant and dangerous prisoner, and he will only answer if she tells him something true about herself in return.
prompt: Quid pro quo: tell me something true about yourself that I don't know yet.
followUps: What would you want to know about me in exchange?
What do you never tell on a first date?

moment: Clarice tells him about the night, as a child, when she heard lambs crying on a farm and tried to save one.
prompt: Which childhood memory still comes back to you at night?
followUps: Who or what did you try to save as a kid?
Which moment made you who you are?

moment: Clarice keeps working in rooms full of men who doubt her, and quietly proves them wrong.
prompt: When did you have to prove yourself in a room where nobody expected much from you?
followUps: Who underestimated you the most?
How do you stay calm when you're being judged?

moment: In a few minutes we watch Carl and Ellie's whole marriage: their first house, and the jar of savings for a trip to South America that keeps getting broken open for real-life emergencies.
prompt: What is our 'Paradise Falls', the trip we keep postponing? What keeps getting in the way?
followUps: Which emergencies have eaten your savings?
What would make you finally book it?

moment: Carl, now an old widower, ties thousands of balloons to his house and flies away rather than give it up.
prompt: If you could take one place with you anywhere, which would it be?
followUps: Which object would you save from your home?
Where would you fly to?

moment: Carl finally opens Ellie's adventure book and finds she filled the last pages with their ordinary days together, and a note telling him to go have a new adventure.
prompt: Which ordinary days with someone turned out to be your greatest adventure?
followUps: Which small daily moment with me would you put in a scrapbook?
What adventure should we start next?

moment: Chihiro, a sulky ten-year-old moving to a new town, wanders into a strange spirit world after her parents eat food that wasn't meant for them.
prompt: What was the move or big change you resisted most as a kid?
followUps: How did you make your first friend in a new place?
What did you lose when you moved?

moment: To survive, Chihiro signs a work contract, and the boss takes her name, leaving her only 'Sen'. Her friend Haku warns her never to forget her real name.
prompt: Which part of yourself do you never want to lose, whatever job or relationship you're in?
followUps: Has a job ever made you forget who you are?
Who reminds you of your real name?

moment: Chihiro remembers falling into a river as a little girl, and realizes her friend Haku is that river.
prompt: Which place from your childhood feels like it looked after you?
followUps: Where did you feel safest as a kid?
Which of those places would you take me to?

moment: WALL-E has spent years cleaning up an empty Earth alone, collecting little treasures and watching an old musical every night, dreaming of holding someone's hand.
prompt: Which little 'treasures' do you keep that would mean nothing to anyone else?
followUps: What would be in your collection?
Which old film or song do you play on repeat?

moment: When EVE arrives, WALL-E falls for her instantly and follows her across the universe, though at first she barely notices him.
prompt: Have you ever followed someone, or a dream, much further than was sensible?
followUps: How long would you wait for someone to notice you?
What's the bravest thing you've done for a crush?

moment: On a giant spaceship full of people who never look up from their screens, two passengers bump into each other and suddenly notice the stars.
prompt: When did you last put your phone down and really notice what was around you?
followUps: What would we do with a screen-free weekend?
Which habit of ours would you swap for looking up?

moment: Woody has always been the favorite, until a shiny new space ranger arrives on Andy's birthday and everybody loves him instead.
prompt: When did you feel replaced by someone new? How did you handle it?
followUps: Have you ever been jealous of a friend's new friend?
What makes you feel secure in a relationship?

moment: Buzz is convinced he is a real space hero, and the moment he sees a TV ad calling him a toy, his world falls apart.
prompt: What did you believe about yourself that one day turned out not to be true?
followUps: What helped you get back up?
Is it better to dream big or to know your limits?

moment: Woody and Buzz, rivals at first, end up teaming up to get home before the moving van leaves.
prompt: Who started out as a rival and became one of your best friends?
followUps: What does it take for you to trust someone you didn't like?
What would we be like as a team on a mission?

moment: Inside eleven-year-old Riley's head, Joy, Sadness, Anger, Fear and Disgust share one control panel, and Joy always tries to run the show.
prompt: Which emotion is at the controls in your head most days? And in mine?
followUps: Which emotion do you hide?
Which one would you fire?

moment: Riley's family moves to a new city, and her happiest memories start turning blue.
prompt: Which happy memory of yours became bittersweet over time?
followUps: Do you prefer to remember or to forget the hard parts?
Which memory of us would you keep forever?

moment: Joy finally understands that it was Riley's sadness that made her parents come and comfort her.
prompt: When has letting yourself be sad brought you closer to someone?
followUps: How do you like to be comforted?
Do you find it hard to let others see you sad?

moment: Miguel dreams of becoming a musician, but in his family music has been banned for generations.
prompt: What dream did your family not support? Did you follow it anyway?
followUps: What did your family forbid that you secretly loved?
Which family rule would you break?

moment: On the Day of the Dead, Miguel learns that people stay alive in the Land of the Dead only as long as someone still remembers them.
prompt: Who do you keep alive by remembering them? Tell me a story about them.
followUps: How do you want to be remembered?
Which family stories should never be lost?

moment: Miguel sings an old lullaby to his great-grandmother Coco, and she, who barely remembers anything anymore, starts singing along.
prompt: What song or ritual connects you to an older person in your family?
followUps: What would you sing to bring back someone's memory?
What do you want to ask your grandparents while you still can?

moment: Mitsuha, a girl from the countryside, and Taki, a boy from Tokyo, randomly wake up in each other's bodies and have to live each other's lives for a day.
prompt: If we swapped lives for a day, what would you do first, and what would you mess up?
followUps: What would you change about my routine?
What would you need to warn me about?

moment: They leave each other notes on their phones and on their hands to keep track, and start falling for someone they have never met.
prompt: Can you fall for someone through their words before you meet them?
followUps: What did you know about me before we met?
What message would you leave me in your handwriting?

moment: Years later, they are both searching for someone without remembering who, until they glimpse each other from two passing trains.
prompt: Do you believe some people are meant to find each other? How did we find each other?
followUps: Have you ever felt you already knew someone?
What would you do if you saw me on a passing train?

moment: Sophie secretly invites three men to her wedding on a Greek island, because her mother's old diary says any of them could be her father.
prompt: If you found your parent's old diary, would you read it?
followUps: What do you think your parents were like at 20?
Which secret would you hope they kept?

moment: Donna sees the three loves of her youth walk onto her island on the same day and has to face who she was back then.
prompt: If all your exes turned up at the same party, how would you feel? What would you say?
followUps: Which past version of you would surprise me?
Which summer changed you?

moment: Sophie decides she doesn't need to know which man is her father, and that maybe she doesn't need to get married at 20 either.
prompt: What did you rush into because you felt you should?
followUps: Which decision are you glad you postponed?
What does 'ready' mean to you?

moment: P. T. Barnum, a poor tailor's son, promises the wealthy girl he loves a life far beyond what her parents expect.
prompt: What big promise did you make when you were young? Did you keep it?
followUps: What would you promise me now?
What did you want to prove to someone's parents?

moment: Barnum brings together people the world had hidden away and turns them into a family of performers.
prompt: Where have you found 'your people', the ones who accept you as you are?
followUps: When did you feel like an outsider?
Who in your circle makes everyone feel welcome?

moment: Chasing fame, Barnum leaves his wife at home while he tours with a famous singer, and almost loses everything.
prompt: When has ambition taken you away from the people you love? What brought you back?
followUps: What would you never sacrifice for success?
How do you notice when you're chasing the wrong thing?

moment: Danny and Sandy had a perfect summer romance, but back at school he acts far too cool to admit he likes her in front of his friends.
prompt: Who were you when nobody from school was watching? Did your friends know the real you?
followUps: What was your teenage group?
Did you ever pretend not to like someone?

moment: Danny and Sandy each tell their friends about their summer together, and the two versions are very different.
prompt: Tell the story of how we met. Then I'll tell my version.
followUps: Which detail do you think I get wrong?
What did your friends hear about me first?

moment: In the end, both change their style for the other: Danny shows up in a varsity sweater and Sandy in head-to-toe leather.
prompt: What have you changed about yourself for someone? Was it worth it?
followUps: What would you never change for love?
What did I change about you, for the better?

moment: Christian, a penniless young writer, arrives in Paris to write about truth, beauty, freedom and love, without ever having been in love.
prompt: What did you think love would be like before you had ever been in love?
followUps: What surprised you most?
Which film or song taught you about love?

moment: Satine, the star of the show, must charm a rich duke to save the theater while secretly falling for the poor writer.
prompt: Have you ever had to choose between what you needed and what you wanted?
followUps: Would you choose stability or passion?
What do you do when love and practicality don't match?

moment: Christian and Satine invent a secret song so they can say 'I love you' in front of everybody without anyone knowing.
prompt: What could be our secret signal for 'I love you' in public?
followUps: Do we already have one?
What would our signal be for 'let's leave this party'?

moment: Furiosa, a truck driver on a supply run, takes a secret detour to drive five women to freedom.
prompt: If you had to cross a desert with only one other person, would you pick me? Who drives?
followUps: What would you pack?
What's our road-trip soundtrack?

moment: Max, a loner who barely speaks, ends up fighting alongside people he just met because they're heading his way.
prompt: Have you ever been helped by a stranger at exactly the right moment?
followUps: Would you trust a stranger in an emergency?
When did you help someone you'd just met?

moment: Furiosa reaches the green place she remembers from childhood and learns it no longer exists. The only way forward is to turn around.
prompt: Have you ever gone back to a place from your past and found it gone? What did you do next?
followUps: Where is 'home' for you now?
When is turning back the brave choice?

moment: Indiana Jones teaches archaeology during the week and spends his holidays escaping booby traps in jungle temples.
prompt: What is your secret second life, the one your colleagues would never guess?
followUps: Which hobby of yours would surprise everyone at work?
What's your most Indiana Jones moment?

moment: Indy is fearless facing a giant rolling boulder, but completely terrified of snakes.
prompt: What is your 'snakes': the small fear that makes no sense next to everything else you can handle?
followUps: Which fear of mine do you find cute?
Would you face it for me?

moment: Marion, whom Indy left years ago, greets him with a punch, then insists on coming along on his adventure.
prompt: How would you react if an ex walked back into your life asking for a favor?
followUps: What do you think about staying friends with exes?
Who from your past would you still help?

moment: Dr. Grant sees a living dinosaur for the first time and has to sit down because his legs give way.
prompt: What sight took your breath away? Where were you?
followUps: Which wonder of the world do you want to see together?
Which childhood obsession would you love to see in real life?

moment: Dr. Grant, who claims he doesn't like kids, ends up protecting two of them through a terrifying night.
prompt: Have you ever ended up taking care of someone you never expected to?
followUps: Do you see yourself as a parent? Why or why not?
What were you like with the kids in your life?

moment: Ian Malcolm warns that the scientists were so busy asking whether they could that they never asked whether they should.
prompt: What did you do just because you could, without asking if you should?
followUps: Which technology would you un-invent?
Where do you draw the line?

moment: Louise, a linguist, is asked to talk to alien visitors and starts with the simplest thing: holding up a whiteboard with her name.
prompt: If you had to introduce humanity with one word or one gesture, what would you choose?
followUps: What's the first word you would teach an alien?
Which gesture means the most to you?

moment: Learning the visitors' language slowly changes the way Louise experiences time.
prompt: Has learning a language or living in another culture changed the way you think?
followUps: Which word from another language do you love?
What would you like us to learn together?

moment: Louise sees the whole of her future, including great pain, and chooses to live it anyway for the love it contains.
prompt: If you knew a love would end in pain, would you still choose it?
followUps: Which joy would you never trade, even knowing the cost?
Would you want to see your future?

moment: Cobb and his team can enter other people's dreams, and each of them carries a small personal object, a totem, to check whether they are awake.
prompt: What would your totem be, the small object that reminds you what's real?
followUps: Which dream do you have over and over?
If you could design one dream, what would it be?

moment: To plant an idea in someone's mind, the team realizes it has to feel like the person's own.
prompt: Which idea did someone plant in your head that you later realized wasn't yours?
followUps: Who has influenced you most without you noticing?
Which idea would you plant in mine?

moment: Cobb and his wife Mal spent what felt like fifty years building a world inside their dreams, and she could not let it go.
prompt: Is there a world, a past or a fantasy, you sometimes prefer to real life?
followUps: What would we build if we could build anything?
How do you come back to reality when it's hard?

moment: Forrest tells his whole life story to strangers on a bench while waiting for the bus, starting with a box of chocolates.
prompt: If you told your life story to a stranger on a bench, where would you start?
followUps: Which chapter would you skip?
What would the stranger remember?

moment: One day Forrest starts running and keeps going for more than three years, and people start following him without knowing why.
prompt: When did you need to just go, without knowing where or why?
followUps: What do you do when your head is full?
Have you ever followed someone without knowing where they were going?

moment: Forrest loves Jenny his whole life, and she keeps leaving and coming back, until she is finally ready.
prompt: Can you love someone who isn't ready yet? How long would you wait?
followUps: What makes someone ready for love?
Were you ready when we met?

moment: Andy, wrongly imprisoned, writes one letter a week asking the state for library books, until years later they finally send them.
prompt: What would you keep asking for, year after year, until you got it?
followUps: What's your most stubborn trait?
What would you build in a place you hated?

moment: Andy plays an opera record over the prison loudspeakers, and every man in the yard stands still to listen.
prompt: When did music stop you in your tracks?
followUps: Which song would you broadcast to everyone?
What do you listen to when you need to feel free?

moment: Red tells Andy that hope is dangerous; Andy answers that hope is maybe the best of things.
prompt: Is hope dangerous or the best thing we have? Where are you on that?
followUps: What are you hoping for right now?
Who keeps your hope alive?

moment: Will, a janitor at a top university, secretly solves the hardest math problem on the hallway blackboard at night.
prompt: Which talent of yours do most people not know about?
followUps: What do you do better than anyone you know?
Who saw your talent first?

moment: Will's therapist Sean tells him that he can quote every book but has never really lived what is in them.
prompt: What do you know a lot about but have never actually experienced?
followUps: Which experience do you want to have rather than read about?
What did you learn only by living it?

moment: Will's best friend tells him the best part of his day is the moment he knocks on Will's door hoping he has left town to use his gift.
prompt: Who in your life wants more for you than you want for yourself?
followUps: What would you push me to do, even if it meant missing me?
Have you ever held yourself back to stay close to your friends?

moment: On one of his first lessons, Mr. Keating makes his students stand on their desks to see the room from a different angle.
prompt: When did you last look at your everyday life from a new angle? What did you see?
followUps: What would you climb on a desk to see differently?
Which teacher changed the way you saw things?

moment: Keating tells the boys to seize the day, and they restart a secret poetry club in a cave at night.
prompt: What secret club would you have started at 17?
followUps: Which rule did you break at school?
What do you want to seize this year?

moment: Neil, who dreams of acting, cannot find the courage to tell his strict father what he really wants.
prompt: What have you never managed to say to a parent?
followUps: What did your parents want you to become?
How would you support me if my family disagreed with my dream?

moment: A chaotic family squeezes into a broken yellow van to drive little Olive across the country to a beauty pageant, and has to push-start it every single time.
prompt: What was the most chaotic family road trip you've ever been on?
followUps: Who was the worst passenger?
What always breaks down on our trips?

moment: Olive's brother Dwayne has stopped talking until he can reach his dream, then finds out he can't, and screams his frustration on the roadside.
prompt: Which dream did you have to let go of? How did you take it?
followUps: Who was there when it happened?
What did you find instead?

moment: When Olive's pageant dance goes wrong, her whole family jumps on stage and dances with her.
prompt: Who would jump on stage with you while you were embarrassing yourself?
followUps: Would you do it for me?
What's your most embarrassing public moment?

moment: Young Toto spends every free moment in the village cinema's projection booth with Alfredo, the projectionist who becomes his friend and father figure.
prompt: Where did you spend all your free time as a child, and with whom?
followUps: Who was your Alfredo?
What was your first film in a cinema?

moment: Alfredo tells the grown-up Toto to leave the village and never come back, because the life he deserves is somewhere else.
prompt: Who pushed you to leave so you could grow? Were they right?
followUps: Would you tell someone you love to leave?
What did you leave behind?

moment: Years later, Toto watches a reel Alfredo left him: all the kissing scenes the village priest had cut from the films.
prompt: What gift has someone made just for you that you will never forget?
followUps: What would you collect for me?
Which moments would be in our reel?

moment: Ofelia, a girl who loves fairy tales, moves with her pregnant mother to her cruel stepfather's army camp, and finds a labyrinth in the woods.
prompt: Which stories helped you escape when real life was hard?
followUps: Which fairy tale did you love as a child?
Where was your hiding place?

moment: Ofelia is warned not to eat anything at a forbidden feast, and she takes two grapes anyway.
prompt: Have you ever broken a rule even though you knew the risk? What made it worth it?
followUps: Which temptation do you never resist?
Are you a rule-follower?

moment: When she is ordered to hand over her baby brother, Ofelia refuses, even though disobeying costs her everything.
prompt: What would you refuse to do, even if it cost you everything?
followUps: Who would you protect without hesitating?
When did you say no to authority?

moment: In 1962 Hong Kong, two neighbors, Mr. Chow and Mrs. Chan, keep passing each other on the narrow stairs down to the noodle stall.
prompt: Who did you see every day without ever really talking to them?
followUps: What's the smallest everyday moment that made your day?
Where would we keep bumping into each other?

moment: Mr. Chow and Mrs. Chan discover that their spouses are having an affair with each other, and promise they will never be like them.
prompt: If you discovered a betrayal like that, what would you do first?
followUps: Can two hurt people become close because of it?
What promise would you make yourself?

moment: They rehearse what they would say to their spouses, and the rehearsals start to feel too real.
prompt: Have you ever rehearsed a hard conversation? Did the real one go as planned?
followUps: Which conversation are you rehearsing now?
Could we rehearse one together?

moment: Philippe, a wealthy man who cannot move his body, hires Driss as his caregiver precisely because Driss doesn't treat him with pity.
prompt: When has someone's honesty helped you more than their kindness?
followUps: Do you prefer gentle or blunt friends?
Who treats you without pity?

moment: Driss pulls Philippe out of his careful routine with fast night drives, paragliding and walks through Paris when he can't sleep.
prompt: Who got you out of a rut and back into life?
followUps: Which adventure would you drag me on?
What do you do when you can't sleep?

moment: Driss secretly arranges for Philippe to finally meet the woman he has been writing letters to for months.
prompt: Who would you trust to push you into meeting someone you're scared to meet?
followUps: Have you ever played matchmaker?
What did it take for us to meet?

moment: Marianne, a painter, is hired to paint Héloïse's wedding portrait without her knowing, so she has to memorize her face on their walks by the sea.
prompt: Which detail of my face or my habits do you know by heart?
followUps: What do you notice about people first?
What would you paint about me?

moment: Héloïse, who never chose her marriage, tells Marianne she has never been to a concert or heard an orchestra play.
prompt: What do you wish you had experienced earlier in life?
followUps: Which experience would you give me if you could?
What did you miss growing up?

moment: Years later, Marianne sees Héloïse across a concert hall, moved to tears by the music they once shared, and Héloïse never looks her way.
prompt: Is there someone you still think of when a certain song plays?
followUps: Which song brings back a whole chapter of your life?
Would you rather remember or forget a lost love?

moment: Phil, a grumpy TV weatherman, wakes up every morning to the same day in the same small town, again and again.
prompt: If you had to relive one ordinary day of your life forever, which would you choose?
followUps: Which day would be a nightmare to repeat?
What would you learn with infinite time?

moment: With endless days on his hands, Phil learns the piano, ice sculpture and the life story of everyone in town.
prompt: What would you learn if you had a year with no consequences?
followUps: What's stopping you from starting now?
What could we learn together?

moment: Phil only escapes the loop when he stops trying to win Rita over and simply becomes a better person.
prompt: What did you have to change in yourself before a relationship could work?
followUps: When did you stop trying to impress me?
What changed in you when we met?

moment: Kat is the most outspoken girl at school, and Patrick, the mysterious bad boy, is secretly paid to date her.
prompt: What reputation did you have at school, and was it fair?
followUps: What did people get wrong about you?
Who would have been paid to date you?

moment: Patrick sings to Kat across the school stadium with the whole marching band behind him, while security chases him.
prompt: What's the most embarrassing romantic gesture you'd be willing to do for me?
followUps: Which grand gesture would mortify you?
Have you ever serenaded someone?

moment: Kat reads a poem in class listing everything she hates about Patrick, and admits the worst part is that she doesn't hate him at all.
prompt: Name three things that annoy you about me, then the one thing that makes it impossible to stay annoyed.
followUps: What's your most annoying habit, honestly?
When did annoyance turn into affection?

moment: Monsieur Gustave, the legendary concierge of a grand mountain hotel, knows every guest's preferences, perfume and secrets.
prompt: If you ran a hotel, what would be your signature detail?
followUps: What do you notice that others forget?
What's the best place you've ever stayed?

moment: Gustave takes Zero, a young lobby boy with no family, under his wing and treats him as his protégé and partner in crime.
prompt: Who took you under their wing when you were starting out?
followUps: Who would you mentor?
What did they teach you?

moment: Thrown in prison, Gustave insists on good manners and civilized conversation with the toughest inmates.
prompt: Which standard of yours do you never drop, even in the worst situation?
followUps: Which small habit keeps you yourself?
What is my non-negotiable?

moment: Andy takes a job as assistant to Miranda Priestly, the terrifying editor of a fashion magazine, without knowing anything about fashion.
prompt: Which job did you take that you were completely unqualified for?
followUps: Who was your worst boss?
What did that job teach you?

moment: To keep up, Andy changes her look, her hours and her priorities, and misses her boyfriend's birthday.
prompt: What did you sacrifice for a job, and was it worth it?
followUps: What would make you quit?
What should a partner say when work takes over?

moment: In Paris, Miranda tells Andy she sees a lot of herself in her, and Andy walks away and tosses her ringing phone into a fountain.
prompt: When did you realize you didn't want to become like someone you admired?
followUps: Who do you secretly want to be like?
What would you throw in the fountain?

moment: Gi-hun, broke and in debt, accepts a stranger's invitation in a subway station to play a children's game for money.
prompt: Which playground game were you unbeatable at?
followUps: What would you do for a huge prize?
Which game would we win as a team?

moment: In one round, players have to pair up first, and only then learn that one person in each pair will lose everything.
prompt: Who would you pick as your partner without knowing what the game was?
followUps: Would you rather play with someone you love or someone strong?
How would you feel if you lost to me?

moment: The players vote to stop the games and go home, then most of them come back, because life outside feels just as hopeless.
prompt: What would make you return to something you swore you'd left behind?
followUps: When does a bad situation feel safer than the unknown?
What do you owe that feels impossible to repay?

moment: The Professor gathers eight robbers who go by city names, Tokyo, Berlin, Nairobi, Rio, and forbids them to share personal details or fall in love.
prompt: If you had a city code name, which would you choose and why?
followUps: Which city would you give me?
Which rule would you break first?

moment: Tokyo and Rio break the no-relationships rule within days.
prompt: Have you ever fallen for someone you really shouldn't have?
followUps: Which rule about love have you broken?
Is a forbidden love more exciting?

moment: The Professor has planned every detail for years, then has to improvise when he falls for the police inspector hunting him.
prompt: Are you a planner or an improviser in love?
followUps: Which plan of yours was ruined by love?
What would you never improvise?

moment: In a small German town, a boy goes missing near a cave, and four families discover they are linked across 1953, 1986 and 2019.
prompt: If you could meet your parents when they were your age, which year would you visit?
followUps: What would you ask them?
What would you never want to find out?

moment: Jonas discovers that the girl he loves is connected to him in a way that makes their relationship impossible.
prompt: What would you do if you found out something about a partner's past that changed everything?
followUps: Is there anything about the past you'd rather not know?
How much of someone's past do you need to know?

moment: People keep trying to change the past, and every attempt causes the very thing they were trying to prevent.
prompt: Have you ever tried so hard to avoid something that you caused it?
followUps: Do you believe in fate?
What would you change if you could go back?

moment: Se-ri, a South Korean heiress, is blown off course while paragliding in a storm and lands in a tree in North Korea, right above a soldier named Jeong-hyeok.
prompt: What's the most unexpected place you've met someone important?
followUps: How did we 'crash land' into each other?
What would you do if you landed somewhere you knew nothing about?

moment: Jeong-hyeok hides Se-ri in his home, and the village women slowly adopt her despite all their suspicions.
prompt: When were you welcomed by people you thought would never accept you?
followUps: How long does it take you to trust new people?
Who in your family would adopt me first?

moment: They fall in love across a border that makes any future together almost impossible.
prompt: What would we do if we lived in two places that made being together almost impossible?
followUps: Could you do long distance?
Which border have you crossed for love?

moment: At 25, Elizabeth suddenly becomes queen when her father dies, and her husband Philip has to walk two steps behind her in public.
prompt: How would you feel if your partner suddenly became far more important than you in public?
followUps: Could you be happy in someone's shadow?
Who is the 'public one' in our relationship?

moment: Princess Margaret is told she cannot marry the man she loves because of rules and duty.
prompt: Would you give up a love because your family or society disapproved?
followUps: Has your family ever disapproved of someone you loved?
What does duty mean to you?

moment: Elizabeth keeps choosing duty over her family's feelings, and her family pays for it over the years.
prompt: What do you do when duty and family pull you in different directions?
followUps: What would you never sacrifice for work?
What did you learn from your parents' choices?

moment: Logan Roy's adult children spend every family dinner competing for who will inherit his media empire.
prompt: What did the siblings or cousins compete for in your family?
followUps: Who was the favorite?
What would we compete for?

moment: Shiv and Tom's marriage is full of strategy, ambition and secrets, and both of them keep score.
prompt: Do you keep score in a relationship? What's on your scoreboard?
followUps: What would a 'fair' relationship look like?
What should never become a competition?

moment: Kendall keeps hoping his father will finally tell him he is proud of him.
prompt: Whose approval are you still waiting for?
followUps: What would you want them to say?
How do you show approval to the people you love?

moment: Carmy, a fine-dining chef, comes home to Chicago to run his late brother's chaotic sandwich shop.
prompt: Which family business or responsibility might you have had to take over?
followUps: What would you cook if you had a restaurant?
What's our signature dish?

moment: In the kitchen everyone shouts 'yes, chef' and works at full speed, while nobody talks about how they actually feel.
prompt: Where in your life do you work hard to avoid feeling things?
followUps: What does your stress look like from the outside?
How can I tell when you're overwhelmed?

moment: Richie, who felt he had no purpose, finds himself while learning to fold napkins and serve guests perfectly at a fine restaurant.
prompt: When did doing something small, very well, change how you saw yourself?
followUps: Which job gave you pride?
What do you do with care that no one notices?

moment: The first time they meet, Sherlock deduces from John's tan and posture that he has just come back from Afghanistan.
prompt: Deduce something about me from what I'm wearing right now.
followUps: What do people guess wrong about you?
What can you read about strangers?

moment: Sherlock calls himself a high-functioning sociopath, but keeps showing he would do anything for John.
prompt: Who in your life acts tough but would do anything for you?
followUps: How do you show care when you're not good with words?
What do you pretend not to feel?

moment: Sherlock fakes his own death to protect his friends and lets John grieve him for two years.
prompt: Would you hide a painful truth from someone to protect them?
followUps: Could you forgive that? How long would it take?
What would you do if I disappeared for two years?

moment: Jay has married Gloria, a much younger Colombian woman, and his adult children are still getting used to it.
prompt: What would your family find hardest to accept about a partner?
followUps: What surprised your family about me?
Does an age gap matter to you?

moment: Phil Dunphy considers himself the 'cool dad' and uses texting slang completely wrong in front of his kids.
prompt: Which of your parents' habits embarrassed you most as a teenager?
followUps: What embarrassing habit will you have as an older person?
What would younger people roll their eyes at about us?

moment: Mitchell and Cam argue about everything, yet they are always the first to show up for each other.
prompt: What do we argue about that doesn't really matter?
followUps: What would you never argue about?
How do we make up?

moment: Jake, the goofiest detective in the precinct, and Amy, the most organized, bet on who will make the most arrests in a year.
prompt: What bet would we make with each other, and what would the loser have to do?
followUps: What's the silliest bet you ever lost?
How competitive are you, honestly?

moment: Captain Holt, who almost never shows emotion, quietly lets his team see how much he cares about them.
prompt: How do you show love without saying it?
followUps: Who in your life shows love in an unusual way?
What tells you that I care?

moment: Every Halloween, the squad turns the precinct into a heist competition to decide who is the ultimate detective and genius.
prompt: If we had a yearly tradition just for us, what would it be?
followUps: Which tradition do you miss?
What new tradition should we start?

moment: After her death, Eleanor wakes up in a perfect neighborhood reserved for good people, and realizes she was let in by mistake.
prompt: If every good deed in your life earned points, what would your score look like?
followUps: What's your best deed that nobody knows about?
What would cost you the most points?

moment: Chidi, a philosophy professor, teaches Eleanor ethics every day, even though he can't decide what to order for lunch.
prompt: How do you make decisions? Are you more Eleanor or Chidi?
followUps: Which decision took you forever?
Which decision did you make in a second?

moment: The group realizes that being good is much easier when you have friends helping you try.
prompt: Who makes you want to be a better person?
followUps: What are you working on in yourself?
How do we help each other grow?

moment: Joel, a hardened survivor, is paid to smuggle a teenage girl, Ellie, across a ruined America, and wants nothing to do with her.
prompt: Who started as an annoying obligation and became important to you?
followUps: What makes you let someone in?
Who did you not want to like at first?

moment: Bill, a lonely survivalist, opens his gate to a stranger named Frank, and they build a whole life together behind the fence.
prompt: What would a good life look like, even if the world was ending?
followUps: What would you grow or build?
What would you want to share with me at the end of the world?

moment: Ellie keeps asking Joel for stories about the world before, and he slowly starts to think about the future again.
prompt: Which part of the world before you were born would you love to have seen?
followUps: What would you tell a kid about our time?
What gives you hope for the future?

moment: Upstairs at Downton lives the aristocratic Crawley family; downstairs, their servants know everything about them.
prompt: If you lived at Downton, would you rather be upstairs or downstairs? Why?
followUps: Which job would you have?
What would the servants gossip about me?

moment: Mary and Matthew, distant cousins thrown together by an inheritance, take years to admit they love each other.
prompt: What's the longest you've taken to admit you liked someone?
followUps: Who made the first move between us?
Why do we hide feelings?

moment: The Dowager Countess delivers a sharp one-liner at every dinner, but always defends her family in the end.
prompt: Who is the sharp-tongued but loyal one in your family?
followUps: What did they say that you still quote?
Which of their qualities do you have?

moment: Otis, the awkward son of a sex therapist, starts running a secret advice clinic for classmates in an abandoned school toilet block.
prompt: What advice were you always asked for as a teenager?
followUps: Who did you go to for advice?
What advice would you give your teenage self?

moment: Otis and Maeve run the clinic together and spend a whole season missing the right moment to tell each other how they feel.
prompt: What moment did you miss with someone because of bad timing?
followUps: Which message would you take back?
How did timing work in our favor?

moment: Eric, Otis's best friend, stops hiding who he is, and his family has to learn to keep up.
prompt: When did you stop hiding a part of yourself? Who supported you?
followUps: Who did you first tell something important about yourself?
What would you still like to show more of?

moment: Wednesday Addams arrives at a new school and makes it clear within five minutes that she is not there to make friends.
prompt: How do you act on your first day in a new group? Open book or closed door?
followUps: How did people see you on your first day at work?
What's your 'go away' face?

moment: Her cheerful roommate Enid keeps trying to be friends, and slowly wins her over.
prompt: Who broke through your walls?
followUps: What finally made you open up?
Are you the Enid or the Wednesday?

moment: Wednesday dances alone at the school dance, a routine so strange that it becomes legendary.
prompt: Would you dance alone in front of everybody? What would your dance look like?
followUps: What makes you stop caring what others think?
Show me your signature move.

moment: Aang wakes up after a hundred years frozen in an iceberg and learns that the world he knew is gone and that he is expected to save it.
prompt: If you woke up after 100 years, what would you look for first?
followUps: Who would you miss?
What would you hope had changed?

moment: Zuko, a banished prince, is obsessed with capturing the Avatar to win back his father's love.
prompt: What did you try too hard to prove to someone?
followUps: Who did you most want to impress?
When did you stop?

moment: Uncle Iroh keeps offering Zuko tea, patience and advice, even after Zuko betrays him.
prompt: Who stayed patient with you when you didn't deserve it?
followUps: Who would you be an Iroh for?
What would you say to them now?

moment: Amir and Hassan fly kites over Kabul, and Hassan always knows exactly where a cut kite will land.
prompt: Who knew you so well as a child that they could predict your next move?
followUps: What did you do on weekends growing up?
What do I always predict about you?

moment: Amir sees his best friend being hurt and does nothing, and the guilt follows him for decades.
prompt: Is there a moment you didn't stand up for someone that you still think about?
followUps: What would you do differently?
How do you forgive yourself?

moment: Years later, Amir is told there is a way to be good again, and he travels back into danger to make things right.
prompt: What would you go back to fix, if you had the chance?
followUps: Who do you owe an apology?
Is it ever too late?

moment: Offred, living under a regime that has taken away women's names and freedoms, remembers small things like having her own bank card and going for a run alone.
prompt: Which small freedom do you take for granted every day?
followUps: What would you miss first?
Which freedom did older generations not have?

moment: Offred finds a message scratched inside her wardrobe by the woman who lived there before her, in mock Latin: don't let the bastards grind you down.
prompt: What phrase keeps you going when things are hard?
followUps: Who taught it to you?
What would you leave scratched in a wardrobe for the next person?

moment: In a world where every gesture is watched, Offred risks a secret relationship with Nick.
prompt: How much would you risk for a moment of real connection?
followUps: When did you take a risk for love?
Can love be an act of rebellion?

moment: At 37, Toru hears a Beatles song on a plane and is instantly back in Tokyo at 19, walking through a meadow with Naoko.
prompt: Which song sends you straight back to being 19?
followUps: Where were you at 19?
Who were you with?

moment: Toru is torn between quiet, fragile Naoko and loud, funny, very alive Midori.
prompt: Are you drawn to quiet depth or bright energy? What does that say about you?
followUps: Which one am I?
What have your past choices taught you?

moment: Naoko asks Toru to always remember her: that she existed, and that she was by his side.
prompt: What do you hope the people from your past remember about you?
followUps: Who do you never want to forget?
What do you want me to remember?

moment: On a misty morning in Barcelona, Daniel's father takes him to the Cemetery of Forgotten Books, where he must choose one book to protect for life.
prompt: If you could protect one book or film forever, which would you choose?
followUps: Which book changed your life?
Which story would you save from being forgotten?

moment: Daniel discovers that someone has been finding and burning every copy of the novel he loves.
prompt: What would you protect from disappearing, even if it put you in danger?
followUps: What's worth defending?
Which memory would you hate to lose?

moment: Daniel uncovers the story of a forgotten author whose life looks strangely like his own.
prompt: Whose life story feels a bit like yours?
followUps: Which older person's story would you love to know?
What would you not want to repeat from their life?

moment: Tita, the youngest daughter, is forbidden to marry because tradition says she must care for her mother, so she pours all her feelings into her cooking.
prompt: What dish would you cook to tell someone how you feel?
followUps: Who cooked with love for you?
What do you cook when you're sad?

moment: Everyone who eats Tita's food feels exactly what she felt while cooking it, from sadness to desire.
prompt: If people could taste your mood in your cooking, what would dinner taste like today?
followUps: Which feeling would you love to share?
Which meal reminds you of a person?

moment: Pedro marries Tita's sister just to stay close to Tita, and they spend years under the same roof.
prompt: Would you rather have someone close but impossible, or far away but free?
followUps: Is that romantic or unfair?
What would you have done in Pedro's place?

moment: Ifemelu leaves Nigeria to study in the US and discovers that there, for the first time, people see her first of all as Black.
prompt: When did you first realize how others saw you from the outside?
followUps: What surprised you most about living somewhere new?
What did living abroad teach you about your own country?

moment: Ifemelu starts an anonymous blog about everything she observes, and it becomes a huge success.
prompt: If you wrote an honest anonymous blog, what would it be about?
followUps: What do you observe that nobody talks about?
Would you tell people it's you?

moment: After fifteen years apart, Ifemelu returns to Lagos and meets Obinze, her first love, who is now married.
prompt: What would you do if you met your first love again after fifteen years?
followUps: What do you still carry from your first love?
What feels unfinished in your life?

moment: Ryland Grace wakes up alone on a spaceship with no memory of who he is or why he's there, and has to figure it out with science.
prompt: If you woke up with no memory, which skill would come back first?
followUps: What do you know without thinking?
Which clue would tell you who you are?

moment: Light-years from home, Ryland meets an alien engineer, and they become best friends by building a shared language from scratch.
prompt: Have you become close to someone who didn't speak your language? How?
followUps: What do you communicate without words?
What would you teach first?

moment: Ryland remembers that he did not volunteer for the mission, and now has to decide whether to be brave this time.
prompt: Can you become brave after failing to be brave the first time?
followUps: When did you find your courage late?
What would you do for a friend at the cost of going home?

moment: Victor Frankenstein works alone night after night, so obsessed with his experiment that he cuts himself off from family and friends.
prompt: Which obsession has made you disappear from people's lives for a while?
followUps: Who pulled you back?
What are you obsessed with right now?

moment: Abandoned by his maker, the creature teaches himself to speak and read by secretly watching a family through a crack in a cottage wall.
prompt: Who did you learn the most from just by watching?
followUps: Which family did you observe and wish you had?
What did you teach yourself?

moment: The creature asks Victor for only one thing: a companion, so that he will not be alone.
prompt: Is loneliness the worst thing a person can feel? What helps you with it?
followUps: When did you feel loneliest?
What does companionship mean to you?

moment: Jonathan Harker travels to a remote castle for a business deal, and slowly realizes his host never eats, casts no reflection, and keeps every door locked.
prompt: What's the strangest place you've stayed for work or travel?
followUps: Which red flag did you ignore once?
When did you know you had to leave?

moment: Mina and Jonathan write letters and keep diaries, and in the end those papers save everyone.
prompt: Do you keep a diary or old messages from people you love? What's in them?
followUps: What letter would you love to receive?
Would you let me read your old diary?

moment: A group of friends make a pact to stand together against something terrifying, whatever the cost.
prompt: Which friends would you trust to face a nightmare with you?
followUps: What role would you play in the group?
Which fear would you face for them?

moment: Feyre, a poor young huntress keeping her family alive, kills a wolf in the woods and is taken away to a faerie land as payment.
prompt: What would you do to keep your family going if things got desperate?
followUps: Who depended on you growing up?
What responsibility came to you too early?

moment: Feyre falls for Tamlin, a powerful faerie lord, who protects her by keeping her locked away.
prompt: Where is the line between protecting someone and controlling them?
followUps: How do you like to be protected?
What would feel like too much?

moment: Feyre realizes that the person who truly sees her is not the one she thought, but someone she first saw as a villain.
prompt: Have you ever misjudged who was really on your side?
followUps: What did someone see in you that others missed?
Who was the 'villain' you misjudged?

moment: Violet trained her whole life to be a scribe, but her mother forces her into a war college for dragon riders where many students don't survive.
prompt: When were you pushed into something you didn't choose? How did you find your way?
followUps: What did your parents choose for you?
What would you have chosen instead?

moment: Violet's greatest enemy at school is Xaden, whose family was destroyed by hers, and they can't stay away from each other.
prompt: Could you love someone whose family hurt yours?
followUps: Have families ever stood in the way for you?
What would make you cross that line?

moment: A dragon chooses Violet not despite her fragility but because of the strength she shows with it.
prompt: Which of your 'weaknesses' turned out to be a strength?
followUps: Which strength do you see in me that I don't?
When did being different help you?

moment: Liesel, a foster girl in Nazi Germany, steals her first book before she can even read.
prompt: What did you take or keep as a child that meant the world to you?
followUps: What was your first favorite book?
Who taught you to read?

moment: Her foster father Hans teaches her to read at night in the basement, painting words on the wall.
prompt: Who stayed up late to teach you something?
followUps: What would you love to teach me?
Where did you learn the most?

moment: Liesel's family hides Max, a young Jewish man, in their basement, and she brings him descriptions of the weather because he cannot see the sky.
prompt: If someone couldn't go outside, how would you describe today's weather to them?
followUps: Who would you risk everything to protect?
Which small gift has meant the most to you?

moment: Ove, a grumpy widower, patrols his street every morning to check that everyone follows the rules on parking and recycling.
prompt: Which rule makes you grumpy when others break it?
followUps: What would you patrol in our home?
Who is the Ove of your street?

moment: A chaotic young family moves in next door and keeps knocking on Ove's door, until he can't help helping them.
prompt: Who kept knocking on your door until you let them into your life?
followUps: Which neighbor do you remember fondly?
How do you help people while pretending to be annoyed?

moment: Ove still talks to his late wife Sonja every day; she was the only color in his black-and-white life.
prompt: Who brings color to your black-and-white days?
followUps: What did the people you loved change about you?
What color am I in your life?

moment: Alex, the US president's son, and Prince Henry of England can't stand each other, until they crash into a royal wedding cake together in front of the world's cameras.
prompt: Who did you think you couldn't stand before you got to know them?
followUps: What's your most public embarrassing moment?
What did you think of me at first?

moment: Alex and Henry keep their relationship secret with endless late-night emails, quoting famous historical love letters to each other.
prompt: Which message or letter from someone have you kept for years?
followUps: What would you write to me in a love letter?
Do you prefer calls, texts or letters?

moment: Their private emails are leaked, and both have to decide whether to hide or let the world see them together.
prompt: Which part of yourself would you defend in front of the whole world?
followUps: What would we do if our private messages became public?
What makes you proud to be with someone?
